why_a_narrow_boundary_is_required.concrete_failure: untracked Pyright configuration and repository-root .pyi providers can reduce Official reportMissingImports to zero while required runtime distributions remain absent
why_a_narrow_boundary_is_required.git: records the files as untracked but does not decide whether they invalidate evaluator meaning
why_a_narrow_boundary_is_required.version_numbers: identify software versions but do not constrain repository workspace effects
why_a_narrow_boundary_is_required.primary_keys: do not express shell or evaluator semantics
why_a_narrow_boundary_is_required.transactions: can make writes atomic but cannot distinguish a runtime provider from a type-only substitute
why_a_narrow_boundary_is_required.unique_constraints: prevent duplicate records, not invalid evaluation artifacts
why_a_narrow_boundary_is_required.types: Pyright itself accepts the type-only providers that cause this false pass
why_a_narrow_boundary_is_required.ordinary_tests: the public goal and Official evaluator both pass in the observed failure

mechanism_findings: V5 model-visible frontier snapshots accumulated in the stateless API context; Meerkat consumed 11706962 prompt tokens versus 5919371 for the matched Minimal-B retry
a replay-passing program can be lost at the final request because the old protocol separates certification from delivery
Official success and deployment validity or completeness must be reported on separate axes
decision: reject V5 as the paper method; retain it as a development baseline and qualify a simpler validity-aware live compatibility frontier that exposes only the newest valid state and returns a clean-replay-passing program immediately
claim_boundary: No success-rate, SOTA, or generalization claim is supported by this consumed development study.
